decision: How should the new section show what your child will work on (math and reading, ages 6-12)?
primary_axis: representation of the skill list: filtered list vs full map vs book artifact
invariants: same headline, lead and skill copy (research/math-reading-offer.md)
same curriculum line: Matched to your province's curriculum + BC AB SK MB ON chips

options.bet: Parent picks their child's age; Math and Reading show side by side for that age
options.benefit: Shortest read; the parent sees only their child's skills
options.cost: Hides the full range; one more interaction
options.risk: Parents who do not click see only ages 8-9

options.bet: The whole map at once: ages across, subjects down, a pencil line showing progression 6 to 12
options.benefit: Shows breadth and progression at a glance; nothing hidden
options.risk: Reads as a curriculum document; on phones it becomes accordions

options.bet: Show the skills as the contents page of a real workbook; age and subject pills change the page
options.benefit: Tangible: ties skills to the paper product and to 'see a sample page'
options.cost: Most custom visual; one subject at a time
options.risk: Page numbers and 'contents' may read as a fixed book, against 'made for one child'
